evidence_summary: The decision rule is implemented as a conjunction: 'all_co_primaries_pass=p1.passes and p2.passes and p3.passes' (src/npl/verdict.py:201). A Sidak correction is a union-type adjustment: it controls the probability that at least one of several tests rejects. Under an all-must-pass (intersection-union) rule the GO decision rejects only when every component rejects, so its type-I error under any configuration in which at least one component null is true is bounded by the LARGEST per-component level, and no correction is required. Applying Sidak therefore makes each component strictly harder and the GO strictly harder than the registered family-wise budget requires. The same repository applies the correct reasoning to its successor hypotheses - 'H2 and H3 require every co-primary (the weakest governs); H4's grid is disjunctive within the hypothesis (Sidak-corrected), so its best cell governs' (src/npl/register/cull.py:18-20, implemented at cull.py:135-144) - and applies no within-hypothesis correction to H2's two required co-primaries, reserving Sidak for H4's union of three cells (register/conditioning.py:sidak_within; registrations/H4/REGISTRATION.md:79-80). H1 is the only place in the program where a union correction is attached to a conjunction. Direction: the correction makes the conjunction harder to pass, i.e. makes the FAIL that H1 fired easier to reach, which is why the direction is A rather than B.
